summary: Fiji is one of the most open countries in the Pacific: citizens of more than a hundred countries — the whole EU, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, most of the Commonwealth and every Pacific Islands Forum neighbor — receive a free four-month visitor permit on arrival, while everyone else must apply to the Fiji Immigration Department before traveling.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, which for most visitors only matters if the trip routes through South America or Africa. No vaccination is required for arrivals from Australia, New Zealand, Asia, North America or Europe.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Fiji. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

onwardTicket.text: At border control visitors must show an onward or return ticket and a valid visa for the next country they are travelling to. Fiji's immigration ministry likewise asks for an onward ticket for the next destination after Fiji.

source.name: UK FCDO — Fiji travel advice (entry requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors are expected to show sufficient funds to support themselves without working. A card statement or cash is enough. No fixed figure is published, and in practice officers only ask when the stay is long or the itinerary is vague.

source.name: Fiji Ministry of Immigration — Frequently asked questions

declarations.name: Fiji Arrival Card and Biosecurity Declaration
declarations.text: Every arriving passenger is given a passenger arrival card, a legal document that is also the biosecurity declaration. All food, plants and plant products, animal products and used materials must be declared or dropped in the amnesty bins; undeclared items found in your baggage bring an on-the-spot fine of FJD 400, and prosecution can lead to a fine of up to FJD 20,000, six months in prison, or both.

source.name: Biosecurity Authority of Fiji — Traveling to Fiji (passenger arrival card)

currencyLimits.text: Amounts of FJD 10,000 or more in cash (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and departure.

source.name: UK FCDO — Fiji travel advice (entry requirements)

notes: The UK Foreign Office says Fiji customs has strict quarantine regulations: officers X-ray all luggage arriving at Nadi airport and confiscate most fresh foodstuffs, unless you are arriving from a country with a quarantine agreement with Fiji.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says credit cards are accepted by most hotels, restaurants and shops, and that ATMs are widely available in main centres and some rural areas; some taxis only take cash. The UK Foreign Office adds that not all ATMs accept the full range of cards, and that hospitals usually ask for immediate cash payment.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says the risk of serious crime is generally low, but there are occasional incidents including sexual assault, and advises care with belongings in cities and popular tourist destinations. It warns of dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries, says cyclones occur throughout the year although the season normally runs from November to April, and notes that healthcare facilities are limited.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Fiji travel advice

tips.text: The Government of Canada says the rainy and cyclone season runs from November to April, and the UK Foreign Office notes that cyclones can occur throughout the year. Cyclones can cause flooding and landslides that block roads, including access to the airport, so keep an eye on forecasts and make sure your insurance covers weather disruption.

The UK Foreign Office says healthcare facilities in Fiji are limited and people are often evacuated to another country for treatment in serious emergencies, and that hospitals usually ask for immediate cash payment. The Government of Canada advises insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

The UK Foreign Office advises covering your shoulders and knees in rural villages and during kava ceremonies, and notes that topless bathing and public nudity are illegal. If you are invited to drink kava, be aware of the potential risk of liver toxicity.
Visa-exempt visitors are granted a free visitor permit of up to four months on arrival, which can be extended to a maximum of six months in any twelve.

The UK Foreign Office warns of dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries. Unless you have reliable local knowledge, swim from beaches with lifeguards on duty and follow the flag warning system.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Fiji?
faq.answer: Probably not. More than a hundred nationalities — all EU and EEA states, the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, India, most Commonwealth countries and every Pacific Islands Forum neighbor — get a free visitor permit stamped on arrival for up to four months. If your country is not on that list you must apply to the Fiji Immigration Department before you travel; there is no visa on arrival for non-exempt nationalities.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Fiji?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt visitors are normally granted four months on arrival; ordinary Chinese passports get a shorter 30-day stay under the Fiji–China agreement. That can be extended in further blocks at an Immigration office, but the total visitor stay is limited to six months within any twelve-month period, after which you need a different permit category.

faq.question: What do I need to show at Fijian immigration?
faq.answer: A passport valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay, a confirmed onward or return ticket, the address of your first accommodation, and a completed arrival card with the biosecurity declaration. Officers may also ask how you will fund the stay.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Fiji?
faq.answer: No official source we could read requires it. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

faq.question: When is cyclone season in Fiji and should I avoid it?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada gives the rainy and cyclone season as November to April, but the UK Foreign Office notes that cyclones can occur throughout the year. Cyclones can bring strong winds, heavy rain, flooding and landslides that block roads, including to the airport. If you travel in those months, choose flexible tickets and insurance that covers weather disruption.
